property_summary: For any recipient and any starting reward, calling withdrawReward(recipient) on the correct contract always sets rewardsForA[recipient] to 0 after the call completes; the mutant that zeroes the balance only after the external call can be re-entered and leave rewardsForA[recipient] nonzero for some inputs (an attacker contract and initial reward).

For any recipient, after calling withdrawReward(recipient) the reference contract always leaves rewardsForA[recipient] == 0 (no residual reward), whereas the mutant that zeroes after the external call can be re-entered by a malicious recipient so that rewardsForA[recipient] remains nonzero.

For every recipient, after calling withdrawReward(recipient) the reference contract always leaves rewardsForA[recipient] equal to 0; the mutant that zeroes the balance after the external call can be re-entered by a malicious recipient so that rewardsForA[recipient] remains nonzero for some inputs.

For any recipient and any initial rewardsForA[recipient], calling withdrawReward(recipient) on the correct contract always results in rewardsForA[recipient] == 0 after the call completes; the mutant that zeroes the storage only after the external call can be re-entered by a malicious recipient so that after withdrawReward returns the stored rewardsForA[recipient] is still non-zero.

For any recipient, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) on the correct contract always results in rewardsForA[recipient] == 0 after the external withdraw completes (the contract prevents reentrancy), but the mutant that zeros rewards after the external call can be re-entered by a malicious recipient to leave rewardsForA[recipient] non-zero.

For any recipient and attacker contract, a single call to withdrawReward(recipient) from C should leave rewardsForA[recipient]==0 (i.e., no funds remain owed) — the mutant that never sets the lock to true can be re-entered by a malicious recipient and thus can leave rewardsForA[recipient] nonzero after withdrawReward returns.

For any recipient, after calling withdrawReward(recipient) the contract's rewardsForA[recipient] must always be zero (the reference prevents reentrancy and clears the pending reward), whereas the mutant that fails to set the lock to true allows a re-entrant recipient to re-enter and leave rewardsForA[recipient] > 0 for some inputs.

For any recipient and any initial reward amount, after calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) (which credits and immediately withdraws a 100-unit bonus), the reference contract always leaves rewardsForA[recipient] == 0 (no pending reward remains); the mutant that fails to set the reentrancy lock can be re-entered by a malicious recipient during the low-level call and can cause rewardsForA[recipient] to remain nonzero for some inputs.

For any recipient address, after calling withdrawReward(recipient) the reference contract always leaves address(c).balance decreased by exactly the withdrawn amount and rewardsForA[recipient] cleared (observable as withdraw call succeeding and leaving c.balance reduced); the mutant allowing reentrancy can be re-entered by a malicious recipient causing withdraw to behave differently (e.g., leave c.balance larger than expected) for some inputs.

For any recipient attacker contract A and any initial reward amount x >= 0, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(A) on the correct contract always results in rewardsForA[A] being zero after the call (no pending reward remains); the mutant that never sets the reentrancy lock can be re-entered by A during the low-level call and can leave rewardsForA[A] > 0 for some inputs.

After calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) the recipient's balance increases by exactly 100 Ether (the bonus) and claimedBonus becomes true before any withdrawal attempt can be prevented by reentrancy.
Calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus on any address never reverts (i.e., completes) when that address is not already marked as having claimed the bonus.

When getFirstWithdrawalBonus is called on an address that has not yet claimed the bonus, the call must not revert (i.e., it completes) for any recipient and any contract balance/state the caller can arrange under the precondition.
If the recipient is an EOA (not a contract) and has not yet claimed the bonus, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus should not revert.
For any recipient that is a contract which does not revert when receiving Ether, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus should not revert.

For any recipient address, after calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) the reference contract always resets rewardsForA[recipient] to 0 (because withdrawReward is called while the bonus is still unclaimed), whereas the mutant that marks claimedBonus before withdrawal can leave rewardsForA[recipient] nonzero when the external call reverts — so there exists an adversarial callee that makes the mutant leave a nonzero reward while the reference still leaves 0.

For any recipient address and attacker behavior, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) on the correct contract always results in rewardsForA[recipient] == 0 after the call completes; the mutant that marks claimedBonus before the external withdrawal can leave rewardsForA[recipient] > 0 for some attacker callee that reverts the withdrawal.

For any recipient and any callee behavior, after a call to getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) on the correct contract, rewardsForA[recipient] is guaranteed to be 0 (because withdrawReward is invoked while the bonus is still claimable), whereas the mutant that marks claimedBonus before calling withdrawReward can leave rewardsForA[recipient] > 0 when the external transfer to the recipient fails — so the invariant rewardsForA[recipient] == 0 always holds on the reference but is violated by the mutant for some adversarial recipient.

For every recipient and any callee behavior, after getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) returns successfully on the reference contract, claimedBonus[recipient] is true (the bonus is marked claimed); the mutant can leave claimedBonus false for some adversarial reverter because it marks claimed before withdrawal and a failing external call can revert the whole transaction causing different observable behavior when using a callee that causes the withdrawal to revert via a fallback that consumes gas and then revert — we detect this by calling through a helper that reverts during receive and observing the final claimedBonus getter on success/failed attempt.

For every recipient and any callee behavior, if getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) returns successfully on the reference C then claimedBonus[recipient] becomes true; the mutant that sets claimedBonus before the external withdraw can cause the call to revert and thus for some adversarial callee the reference will return true while the mutant's call will revert (observable via success flag).
After calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) once, the contract's ETH balance decreases by at least 100 (i.e., the bonus is immediately paid out).
